papers.title: Seroepidemiology of Enterovirus D68 in Xiamen Children: A Cross-Sectional Study in 2022
papers.abstract: Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) is a re-emerging pathogen associated with severe acute flaccid myelitis (AFM) and pneumonia, predominantly in children but also capable of causing severe disease in immunocompromised adults. Seroprevalence data are essential for understanding population immunity, age-specific susceptibility, and viral transmission dynamics; yet, such data for the period after the COVID-19 pandemic are scarce. We conducted a cross-sectional serological survey to characterize the neutralizing antibody profile of EV-D68 among children in Xiamen, China, in 2022. A total of 453 children aged 0–16 years (217 with acute respiratory tract infection [ARTI] and 236 without) were enrolled. Neutralizing antibody (NtAb) titers against the EV-D68 STL strain were measured using a microneutralization assay, seropositivity was defined as a titer ≥1:16. Multivariable regression and analysis of covariance were used to adjust for age and sex. Overall seroprevalence was 96.0% (435/453), exceeding 90.0% in every age subgroup (0–1 y: 100%; 1–3 y: 97.6%; 3–5 y: 92.6%; ≥5 y: 96.2%). The geometric mean titer (GMT) was 76.78 (95% CI: 68.32–85.24). After adjustment, ARTI status was not significantly associated with seropositivity (adjusted OR = 1.42, 95% CI: 0.46–4.41, p = 0.542). In an exploratory comparison, children with ARTI showed nominally higher antibody titers than those without (Mann–Whitney U test, p = 0.003), although the absence of EV-D68-specific PCR testing precludes etiologic attribution of respiratory symptoms to EV-D68 infection. Infants 90.0%) with distinct age-dependent patterns. These findings provide key reference data for ongoing serosurveillance, outbreak risk assessment, and the evaluation of future vaccines or immunoprophylactic strategies should they become available.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional serological study conducted in Xiamen, China, in 2022 aimed to characterize the neutralizing antibody profile of Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) among children. The study enrolled 453 children aged 0–16 years, with 217 having acute respiratory tract infection (ARTI) and 236 without. Overall seroprevalence was 96.0%, with all age subgroups showing seroprevalence above 90.0%. The geometric mean titer (GMT) was 76.78 (95% CI: 68.32–85.24). Although children with ARTI showed nominally higher antibody titers, the lack of EV-D68-specific PCR testing prevented etiologic attribution. The findings offer critical data for serosurveillance, outbreak risk assessment, and future vaccine development.

papers.title: Disease burden of non-polio enterovirus-associated meningitis in children in G20 countries: an analysis based on GBD data and projections to 2050
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Non-polio enteroviruses (NPEVs) have emerged as the leading etiological cause of childhood meningitis globally, yet the long-term disease burden and its epidemiological trends within G20 countries remain insufficiently characterized. This study aims to systematically evaluate the burden of pediatric NPEV-associated meningitis in G20 countries from 1990 to 2023 and to project future trends to 2050. METHODS: Data were extracted from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 (GBD 2023) database. The primary outcome measures were mortality and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) due to NPEV-associated meningitis in children aged 0-14 years. Estimated annual percentage changes (EAPCs) were calculated to quantify temporal trends. Spearman's rank correlation was used to assess the relationship between disease burden and the Socio-demographic Index (SDI) across G20 countries. A Bayesian age-period-cohort (BAPC) model was employed to forecast disease burden to 2050. RESULTS: In G20 countries, the mortality rate for pediatric NPEV-associated meningitis declined from 1.153 per 100,000 (95% UI: 0.902-1.453) in 1990 to 0.088 per 100,000 (95% UI: 0.070-0.113) in 2023 (EAPC: -7.72%, 95% CI: -8.19 to -7.24). The DALY rate decreased from 107.732 to 9.487 per 100,000 over the same period (EAPC: -7.35%, 95% CI: -7.80 to -6.91). Significant age-related disparities were observed: infants younger than 1 year bore the highest burden (mortality: 0.890 per 100,000; DALY: 80.649 per 100,000), despite showing smaller relative declines compared to older children. At the national level, Indonesia had the highest mortality rate (0.374 per 100,000) and DALY rate (34.344 per 100,000)\. Notably, South Africa exhibited the slowest decline among all G20 members (mortality EAPC: -3.80%; DALY EAPC: -3.76%), far below the G20 averages. Both mortality and DALY rates showed significant negative correlations with SDI across G20 countries (r = -0.849 and - 0.832, respectively, both p < 0.001). Projections to 2050 indicate continued declines, with mortality and DALY rates decreasing by over 95% in G20 countries. CONCLUSIONS: From 1990 to 2023, the burden of pediatric NPEV meningitis in G20 countries declined significantly, yet substantial intra-G20 disparities persist. Indonesia had the highest rates, India the largest absolute numbers, and South Africa the slowest decline. Infants younger than 1 remain the most vulnerable group. Future efforts should prioritize enhanced surveillance and targeted interventions in high-burden countries including Indonesia, South Africa, and India, and strengthen diagnostic capacities in lower-resourced member states to narrow gaps within this influential group of nations.

This study was needed to systematically evaluate the burden of pediatric NPEV-associated meningitis in G20 countries and project future trends to 2050.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed data from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 (GBD 2023) database to assess the burden of NPEV-associated meningitis in children aged 0-14 years across G20 countries from 1990 to 2023.
analysis.methods: Primary outcome measures included mortality and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) due to NPEV-associated meningitis. Estimated annual percentage changes (EAPCs) were calculated to quantify temporal trends, and Spearman's rank correlation assessed the relationship between disease burden and the Socio-demographic Index (SDI). A Bayesian age-period-cohort (BAPC) model was used to forecast disease burden to 2050.
analysis.main_results: From 1990 to 2023, the mortality rate for pediatric NPEV-associated meningitis in G20 countries declined from 1.153 per 100,000 (95% UI: 0.902-1.453) to 0.088 per 100,000 (95% UI: 0.070-0.113) (EAPC: -7.72%, 95% CI: -8.19 to -7.24). The DALY rate decreased from 107.732 to 9.487 per 100,000 (EAPC: -7.35%, 95% CI: -7.80 to -6.91). Infants younger than 1 year had the highest burden (mortality: 0.890 per 100,000; DALY: 80.649 per 100,000).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as a significant decline in NPEV-associated meningitis burden in G20 countries over three decades, with persistent disparities across nations and age groups. The novelty lies in the comprehensive quantification of trends and projections to 2050 using advanced modeling techniques.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform targeted surveillance and intervention strategies in high-burden G20 countries such as Indonesia, South Africa, and India, and highlight the need to strengthen diagnostic capacities in lower-resourced member states to reduce intra-G20 disparities.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on GBD 2023 data, which may have inherent limitations in case ascertainment and representativeness across G20 countries. The evidence strength is high for temporal trends and projections but moderate for causal inference due to ecological study design and potential confounding.

analysis.summary_en: This study systematically evaluated the burden of non-polio enterovirus (NPEV)-associated meningitis in children aged 0-14 years across G20 countries from 1990 to 2023 using Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 data. It quantified mortality and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) and calculated estimated annual percentage changes (EAPCs) to assess temporal trends. A Bayesian age-period-cohort model projected disease burden to 2050. Key findings include a substantial decline in mortality (from 1.153 to 0.088 per 100,000) and DALY rates (from 107.732 to 9.487 per 100,000) over the study period, with infants under 1 year bearing the highest burden. Significant negative correlations between disease burden and Socio-demographic Index (SDI) were observed. Indonesia had the highest rates, India the largest absolute numbers, and South Africa the slowest decline. The study concludes that while progress has been made, substantial disparities persist, necessitating targeted interventions and enhanced surveillance in high-burden countries.

papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Non-polio enteroviruses (NPEVs) have emerged as the leading etiological cause of childhood meningitis globally, yet the long-term disease burden and its epidemiological trends within G20 countries remain insufficiently characterized. METHODS: Data were extracted from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 (GBD 2023) database. The primary outcome measures were mortality and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) due to NPEV-associated meningitis in children aged 0-14 years. Estimated annual percentage changes (EAPCs) were calculated to quantify temporal trends. Spearman's rank correlation was used to assess the relationship between disease burden and the Socio-demographic Index (SDI) across G20 countries. A Bayesian age-period-cohort (BAPC) model was employed to forecast disease burden to 2050. RESULTS: In G20 countries, the mortality rate for pediatric NPEV-associated meningitis declined from 1.153 per 100,000 (95% UI: 0.902-1.453) in 1990 to 0.088 per 100,000 (95% UI: 0.070-0.113) in 2023 (EAPC: -7.72%, 95% CI: -8.19 to -7.24). The DALY rate decreased from 107.732 to 9.487 per 100,000 over the same period (EAPC: -7.35%, 95% CI: -7.80 to -6.91). Significant age-related disparities were observed: infants younger than 1 year bore the highest burden (mortality: 0.890 per 100,000; DALY: 80.649 per 100,000), despite showing smaller relative declines compared to older children. At the national level, Indonesia had the highest mortality rate (0.374 per 100,000) and DALY rate (34.344 per 100,000)\. Notably, South Africa exhibited the slowest decline among all G20 members (mortality EAPC: -3.80%; DALY EAPC: -3.76%), far below the G20 averages. Both mortality and DALY rates showed significant negative correlations with SDI across G20 countries (r = -0.849 and - 0.832, respectively, both p < 0.001). Projections to 2050 indicate continued declines, with mortality and DALY rates decreasing by over 95% in G20 countries. CONCLUSIONS: From 1990 to 2023, the burden of pediatric NPEV meningitis in G20 countries declined significantly, yet substantial intra-G20 disparities persist. Indonesia had the highest rates, India the largest absolute numbers, and South Africa the slowest decline. Infants younger than 1 remain the most vulnerable group. Future efforts should prioritize enhanced surveillance and targeted interventions in high-burden countries including Indonesia, South Africa, and India, and strengthen diagnostic capacities in lower-resourced member states to narrow gaps within this influential group of nations.

papers.title: EVALUATING THE MECHANISMS OF PATHOGENESIS AND ANTIBODY-MEDIATED PROTECTION IN ENTEROVIRUS D68-INDUCED ACUTE FLACCID MYELITIS
papers.abstract: Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) is a major cause of acute flaccid myelitis (AFM), a severe neurologic disease in children that can result in sudden paralysis and lifelong disability. Currently, no approved therapies specifically target EV-D68-associated AFM. Monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) represent a promising therapeutic strategy because they combine viral neutralization through the Fab region with immune-cell recruitment through the Fc region. However, the contribution of Fc effector function to protection against EV-D68-induced neurologic disease remains unclear. This study investigated whether Fc effector function enhances protection against AFM using the partially neutralizing mAb EV68-41. Wild-type EV68-41 (EV68-41-WT), which retains Fc effector function, was compared with an Fc-deficient LALAPG variant (EV68-41-LALAPG) in an animal model of EV-D68 infection. Survival and neurologic outcomes were assessed and compared with the potently neutralizing mAb EV68-228. No significant difference in survival was observed between EV68-41-WT and EV68-41-LALAPG, with both providing approximately 60% survival. However, EV68-41-LALAPG-treated mice exhibited higher peak neurologic scores, indicating more severe limb paralysis, compared with EV68-41-WT-treated mice. In contrast, both EV68-228 variants provided 100% survival and complete neurologic protection. These findings demonstrate that Fc effector function can reduce neurologic disease severity even when it does not significantly improve survival. Together, the results suggest that effective mAb therapies for EV-D68-associated AFM should combine potent viral neutralization with Fc-mediated immune recruitment, potentially improving neurologic outcomes and reducing the burden of childhood paralysis.

papers.source_body_en: Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) is a major cause of acute flaccid myelitis (AFM), a severe neurologic disease in children that can result in sudden paralysis and lifelong disability. Currently, no approved therapies specifically target EV-D68-associated AFM. Monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) represent a promising therapeutic strategy because they combine viral neutralization through the Fab region with immune-cell recruitment through the Fc region. However, the contribution of Fc effector function to protection against EV-D68-induced neurologic disease remains unclear. This study investigated whether Fc effector function enhances protection against AFM using the partially neutralizing mAb EV68-41. Wild-type EV68-41 (EV68-41-WT), which retains Fc effector function, was compared with an Fc-deficient LALAPG variant (EV68-41-LALAPG) in an animal model of EV-D68 infection. Survival and neurologic outcomes were assessed and compared with the potently neutralizing mAb EV68-228. No significant difference in survival was observed between EV68-41-WT and EV68-41-LALAPG, with both providing approximately 60% survival. However, EV68-41-LALAPG-treated mice exhibited higher peak neurologic scores, indicating more severe limb paralysis, compared with EV68-41-WT-treated mice. In contrast, both EV68-228 variants provided 100% survival and complete neurologic protection. These findings demonstrate that Fc effector function can reduce neurologic disease severity even when it does not significantly improve survival. Together, the results suggest that effective mAb therapies for EV-D68-associated AFM should combine potent viral neutralization with Fc-mediated immune recruitment, potentially improving neurologic outcomes and reducing the burden of childhood paralysis.
